**Short answer** > **Take the contract only if you can demonstrate that your group’s *total* Medicare‑Advantage cost per member is ≤ $7,000–$8,000/yr (after accounting for overhead), that you have a mature population‑health platform and risk‑adjustment model, and that stop‑loss coverage can be secured at ≤ $2,800 PMAY.** > In practice most 40‑physician groups will need to negotiate a **hybrid structure**—base capitation + shared savings + carve‑outs—rather than a pure full‑risk deal. --- ## 1. Revised financial snapshot | Item | Estimate for 25 000 members (annual) | |------|-------------------------------------| | Base capitation (1,180 $/PM) | **$351 M** | | Expected total MA cost per member (average) | $7,500–$8,500 → **$187.5–$212.5 M** | | Stop‑loss premium (typical full‑risk PMAY 2,200 $/member) | **$55 M** | | Overhead & operating margin target (10 % of revenue) | **$35 M** | | **Projected net margin before quality bonuses** | **$48–$68 M** | *Key take‑away:* The cap rate alone is higher than the average MA cost, but you must subtract a realistic stop‑loss premium and overhead. A margin of $2,000–$3,000 per member (≈ $50 M annually) is considered attractive for a primary‑care group. --- ## 2. Clinical operations requirements | Requirement | Why it matters | Realistic investment (annual) | |-------------|----------------|--------------------------------| | **Population‑health analytics** | Identify high‑risk patients early and target interventions that reduce costly acute care. | $1–1.5 M for data warehouse, integration with EHR/claims, SDOH feeds. | | **Care coordination & case management** | Reduce ED visits/readmissions—key cost drivers in MA. | 4–6 full‑time care coordinators ($120k each) → $480–$720 k + telehealth platform $200–300 k. | | **Quality measurement infrastructure** | HEDIS bonuses are tied to specific metrics; automated reporting reduces manual effort and risk of penalties. | $250–400 k for dashboards, quality champions, and training. | | **Clinical pathways & protocols** | Standardize care, reduce variation, improve outcomes. | $150–250 k for evidence‑based order sets, CDS integration. | | **Patient engagement tools** | Improves adherence, reduces costs. | $200–350 k for portal enhancements, remote monitoring devices (e.g., BP cuffs). | > **Total clinical ops budget ≈ $2.3–$3.1 M (~9–12 % of projected revenue).** > If you cannot justify this spend, the contract will erode margins. --- ## 3. Legal & regulatory safeguards | Exposure | Mitigation (corrected) | |----------|------------------------| | **Malpractice liability** | Maintain adequate malpractice insurance; include *indemnification clauses that protect the provider* from claims arising from the payer’s actions, not vice‑versa. | | **CMS compliance (Medicare Advantage)** | A dedicated compliance officer is optional unless you have > 50 employees or multiple sites; otherwise rely on the payer’s CMS‑approved data platform and conduct quarterly internal audits. | | **Contractual ambiguity** | Use clear language for risk‑adjustment formulas, stop‑loss triggers, carve‑out definitions, and quality bonus thresholds. | | **Data privacy (HIPAA & HITECH)** | Sign Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with the payer; ensure all data exchanges are encrypted and audit‑ready. | | **Dispute resolution** | First level: Joint Oversight Committee mediation; second level: binding arbitration under the American Arbitration Association. | --- ## 4. Deal‑structure blueprint ### A. Payment model | Component | Detail & Benchmark | |-----------|--------------------| | **Base capitation** | $1,180 PMPM (fixed). | | **Risk adjustment** | CMS HCC weights applied to the base rate; no flat per‑condition add‑on. Example: a patient with 3 chronic conditions may receive an additional 12 % of base ($142/PM). | | **Quality bonus tiering** | • ≥ target → 1–2 % of base (e.g., $3,500 PM).
• > 110 % of target → 3–4 % of base.
• Cap at $35 M annually. | | **Shared‑savings clause** | If total MA cost per member falls below $7,200/PM (≈ $86,400/yr), you share 50 % of the savings with the payer. Threshold and split negotiated in advance. | ### B. Risk protection | Element | Detail | |---------|--------| | **Stop‑loss** | Fixed PMAY negotiated at $2,200–$3,000 per member (≈ 18–25 % of capitation revenue). Payer may require a minimum enrollment period before coverage kicks in. | | **High‑cost carve‑out** | For patients whose annual cost > $25,000 and who receive specialty services (e.g., cardiology, oncology), the payer pays an external provider or hospital network at a negotiated fee. This protects you from catastrophic spikes. | | **Cost‑control caps** | If any single patient’s cost exceeds $50,000/yr, the contract triggers a joint review; if confirmed, the carve‑out applies automatically. | ### C. Governance & oversight 1. **Joint Oversight Committee (JOC)** – 3 members each from your group and the payer; meets quarterly to review performance metrics, risk reports, and quality dashboards. 2. **Data sharing agreement** – Real‑time exchange of claims, EHR data, and SDOH indicators via a secure API; includes audit rights for both parties and explicit data‑ownership clauses (the payer retains ownership of claims data but grants you read/write access to your own patient records). 3. **Audit & compliance schedule** – Annual external audit by an independent CPA to verify cost calculations and quality metrics; internal audit biannually. 4. **Dispute resolution** – First level: JOC mediation; second level: binding arbitration under the American Arbitration Association. ### D. Exit / transition provisions | Scenario | Termination clause | |----------|--------------------| | **Material breach by payer** (e.g., failure to pay on time) | 30‑day cure period, then termination with no penalty. | | **Material breach by group** (e.g., sustained quality shortfalls > 10 % of target for 2 consecutive quarters) | 60‑day notice; option to renegotiate or terminate. | | **Change in ownership / merger** | Payer must obtain written consent; group may elect to exit with a pro‑rata payout based on remaining capitation revenue. | --- ## 5. Decision framework (profitability model) 1. **Projected annual margin per member** \[ \text{Margin} = (\text{Cap rate} - \text{Expected MA cost} - \text{Stop‑loss PMAY}) \times 12 \] 2. **Example calculation** *Cap rate* = $1,180/PM → $14,160/yr *Expected MA cost* = $8,000/yr (includes all services) *Stop‑loss* = $2,200 PMAY → $26,400/yr \[ \text{Margin} = 14,160 - 8,000 - 2,200 = \$3,960\;\text{/member} \] Annual margin for 25 k members ≈ **$99 M** before overhead and quality bonuses. 3. **Thresholds** | Criterion | Target | |-----------|--------| | Margin per member | ≥ $2,000 (≈ $50 M annually) | | Stop‑loss premium | ≤ $2,800 PMAY | | Overhead & operating margin | ≤ 10 % of revenue | | Quality bonus payout | 1–4 % of base (negotiated) | > **If the projected margin meets or exceeds the thresholds above, the contract is financially viable.** > If not, renegotiate cap rate, stop‑loss terms, or consider a hybrid structure. --- ## 6. Final recommendation | Decision | Conditions that must be met | |----------|-----------------------------| | **Proceed with negotiation** | • Current total MA cost per member ≤ $7,500/yr (after overhead).
• Stop‑loss coverage secured at ≤ $2,800 PMAY.
• Mature population‑health platform and validated HCC risk‑adjustment model in place or can be built within 12 months at < 10 % of projected revenue.
• Quality bonus schedule is realistic (1–4 % of base) and shared‑savings threshold aligns with your cost structure. | | **Decline or renegotiate** | • Current MA cost per member > $8,000/yr without clear savings potential.
• Stop‑loss premium > $3,200 PMAY (exceeds 25 % of capitation).
• Payer’s risk‑adjustment formula undervalues your patient mix (e.g., high prevalence of complex chronic disease).
• Legal counsel flags ambiguous carve‑out or liability clauses. | **Bottom line:** A full‑risk capitated contract can be lucrative, but only if you control costs, have a robust quality program, and protect yourself from catastrophic claims. The structure above gives you the flexibility to manage risk while keeping incentives aligned for both clinical excellence and financial sustainability.
